items.title: Adobe Max 2026's lineup tells us a lot about the company's AI priorities right now
items.excerpt: Creative Bloq reads Adobe MAX 2026's session and speaker lineup as a map of where Adobe is steering its creative AI, from Firefly models and agentic assistants inside Photoshop and Premiere to how it pitches AI to working designers.

items.title: Meta's new AI avatar feels like a distraction from the bigger picture
items.excerpt: A design critique of Meta's cute, customisable Muse AI avatar: Creative Bloq argues the character design infantilises users and papers over bigger questions about the agent underneath.

items.title: No, that Apple Games advert isn't AI, and the brilliant BTS video proves it
items.excerpt: Viewers assumed Apple's new Games ad was AI-generated; a behind-the-scenes video shows painstaking hand-made stop-motion craft, a sign of how AI suspicion now shapes how creative work is received.

items.title: Which MCP server can design SVG and app UI? Eight compared (2026)
items.excerpt: A hands-on comparison of eight MCP servers that let coding agents design app UI screens, icons and SVGs, covering which ones output editable design files versus raw code.

items.title: Benchmarking Next-Gen Image & Video Generation in 2026: GPT-Image-2.5 Flare, Grok Imagine 2.0, and 4K Commercial Pipelines
items.excerpt: A practitioner benchmark of the latest image and video generators (GPT-Image-2.5 Flare, Grok Imagine 2.0 and others) for 4K commercial ad pipelines, comparing fidelity, consistency and cost.

items.title: Pixel Canary is now available in stealth for free on AI Gateway
items.excerpt: Vercel's AI Gateway added Pixel Canary, a stealth model free during preview whose stated strengths are coding, frontend development and mobile app design.

items.title: Otoy releases OctaneRender 2027.1 in alpha (updated for Alpha 3)
items.excerpt: OctaneRender 2027.1's experimental build adds a real-time neural rendering mode built on DLSS-style ray reconstruction for near noise-free viewport renders, an updated AI Light system and USD export; Alpha 3 adds SDF-to-mesh baking.

items.title: Bluebeam expands academic access to AI-assisted AEC tools
items.excerpt: Bluebeam is opening its Max tier to eligible students and educators, giving them AI features for document review, design comparisons, markup generation and workflow automation.

items.title: MathWorks introduces MATLAB and Simulink Release 2026b
items.excerpt: Release 2026b adds AI-assisted profiling through Simulink Copilot, a Visual Inspection Toolbox mixing AI and image processing, and PyTorch co-execution for hardware-software co-design workflows.

items.title: Hologram: Meta Is Finally Set To Ship Realistic Avatars, And We Tried Them
items.excerpt: Meta's Hologram realistic avatars, generated by a server-side real-time generative diffusion model from a phone scan, ship shoulders-up on Ray-Ban Display and then full-body in stereo 3D on Meta VR Glasses; UploadVR tried both.

items.title: Meta's next VR device isn't a headset — it's glasses
items.excerpt: Hands-on with Meta VR Glasses, the puck-tethered lightweight successor to Quest: a new form factor that changes what XR prototyping and spatial interface design have to target.

items.title: Meta Launches $1M Developer Competition to Stock 'VR Glasses' with More Hand-tracked Apps
items.excerpt: Meta's new VR Start Developer Competition puts up $1 million to seed hand-tracked apps for Meta VR Glasses, pushing creators toward controller-free interaction design.

items.title: It's sinister that Meta's Muse AI mascot is so cute
items.excerpt: The Verge's Optimizer column examines how Meta uses a cute mascot to make its Muse AI agent easier to accept, and what that character-design strategy hides.

items.title: With Meta's Muse Charm, AI enters its kawaii era
items.excerpt: To sell AI hardware to the masses, Meta is going kawaii: the Muse Charm is a Tamagotchi-like handheld that personifies its Muse agent as a fuzzy, nameable mascot, a deliberate design move against AI's image problem.

items.title: The AI transformation underway at Musinsa
items.excerpt: Inside Korean fashion platform Musinsa's organisation-wide AX program led by two directors: moving past individual ChatGPT proficiency to redesign how teams, including creative and styling work, operate with AI.

items.title: I stopped asking my team to use AI. I asked them to manage it
items.excerpt: A team lead describes reframing AI adoption: employees manage AI agents as teammates with clear roles, reviews and human oversight instead of simply being told to use AI tools.

items.title: You can now chat with Lovable for free
items.excerpt: Lovable opened its chat mode to free users: ask it which idea is worth building, turn customer feedback into a plan, or put it to work on an already-launched app before spending build credits.

items.title: Inside Chats: How Lovable's Agents Work Together
items.excerpt: Lovable explains the architecture behind its multi-agent Chats: trajectories, inboxes, activations and a Git-inspired event log that lets agents stream, fork and survive deploys.

items.title: Meta debuts Tamagotchi-style AI agent
items.excerpt: The Muse Charm, produced by Meta's new design team led by former Apple design chief Alan Dye, puts a customisable cartoon embodiment of the Muse AI agent on a two-inch lanyard device.

items.title: A Trump team wants to automate U.S. Web Design System accessibility testing. Experts are worried.
items.excerpt: GitHub community members and accessibility experts worry that plans to 'automate as much accessibility testing as possible' in the U.S. Web Design System, potentially leaning on AI, could reverse progress in the government's design system.

items.title: AI News: Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, Jev, Muse and More!
items.excerpt: Matt Wolfe's weekly roundup of AI news creators may have missed: Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-Live 1 and the Agent API, Meta's Jev and Muse, and new creative tools.

items.title: Meta is pivoting again... everything you missed from Connect 2026
items.excerpt: Fireship breaks down Meta Connect 2026: Muse AI agent and Charm device, VR Glasses, Hologram avatars and Horizon AI creation tools.

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 AI: An Incredible Leap Forward
items.excerpt: Two Minute Papers walks through Claude Opus 5.5's reported capabilities and experiments, including simulation and agentic tasks.
